title: चीरहरण  उपन्यासमा नारीवादी चेतना {Feminist Consciousness in Chirharan Novel}
nepali: प्रस्तुत अध्ययनमा अस्तित्ववादी नारीवादी सिमोन द बुभोले अघि सारेको नारीवादी विचारलाई आधार बनाएर नीलम कार्की निहारिकाको चीरहरण उपन्यासमा प्रस्तुत नारीवादी चेतनाको निरूपण गरिएको छ । नारीलाई दोस्रो दर्जाका नागरिकमा रूपमा हेर्ने परिपाटीको विरूद्धमा नारी तथा पुरूषपात्रमा जागृत चेतनालाई प्रस्तुत गरिएको यस उपन्यासको नारीवादी विश्लेषणका लागि नारी अस्तित्वप्रतिको चेतना तथा नारीविभेदको विरोधप्रतिको चेतनालाई विश्लेषणका मूल आधार मानिएको छ । नारी अस्तित्वप्रतिको चेतनाभित्र नारीको पहिचान एवम् स्वतन्त्र अस्तित्वप्रतिको चेतना, नारीको वैयक्तिक अधिकारप्रतिको चेतना, पितृसत्तात्मक दमन तथा महिला हिंसाप्रतिको विरोध सम्बन्धी चेतनाका साथै राजनीति र शक्ति संरचनामानारीको समान सहभागिताप्रतिको चेतनालाई र नारीविभेदको विरोधप्रतिको चेतनाभित्र लैङ्गिक विभेदएवम् समानताप्रतिको चेतना, जातीय एवम् वर्गीय विभेदप्रतिको चेतनाका साथै धार्मिक एवम् सांस्कृतिक विभेदप्रतिको चेतनालाई उपन्यास विश्लेषणका ढाँचा मानिएको छ । विवेच्य उपन्यासका सापेक्षमा निर्धारण गरिएका नारीवादी प्रवृत्तिका यी विविध बुँदाहरूका आधारमा उपन्यासका साक्ष्यको विश्लेषणबाट यस उपन्यासमा नारीहरूलाई शारीरिक रूपमा भिन्न भएकैले लैङ्गिक आधारमा विभेद गर्ने, दमन गर्ने, हेप्ने तथा कमजोर मानव ठानी विभिन्न किसिमका हेयपूर्ण उपमा दिने प्रवृत्तिको विरोध गरिएकाले लैङ्गक विभेद र समानताप्रतिको चेतना मुखरित बन्न पुगेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । यस्तै पितृसत्तात्मक समाजमा लिङ्गका आधारमा नारीको बौद्धिकता र क्षमतामाथि बन्देज तथा विभेद गरिने परिपाटीको समेतविरोध गरिएको, नारीलाई धर्म र संस्कृतिले निर्माण गरेका विभिन्न कुरीतिको फन्दामा बेरिने प्रवृत्तिदेखि लिएर राजनीति, शक्तिसम्बन्ध तथा वैयक्तिक निर्णयमा समेत नारीको स्वतन्त्रताको पक्षमा आवाज उठाइएको हुनाले नारी अस्तित्वप्रतिको चेतना तथा नारीविभेदप्रतिको विरोधको चेतना सशक्त बनेको तथ्यपनि प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । महाभारतकालीन समयका पात्र तथा घटनालाई लिएर वर्तमान परिवेशका तादात्म्यमा पुनर्लेखन गरिएको प्रस्तुत उपन्यासमा अस्तित्ववादी नारीवादी प्रवृत्ति सशक्त बन्न पुगेको निष्कर्ष यस अध्ययनले निकालेको छ ।
american_english: In the present study, based on the feminist ideas advanced by existentialist feminist Simone de Beauvoir, the feminist consciousness presented in Neelam Karki Niharika's novel Chirharan is analyzed. For the feminist analysis of this novel, which presents the consciousness awakened in female and male characters against the practice of treating women as second-class citizens, consciousness of female existence and consciousness of resistance to discrimination against women are taken as the core bases of analysis. Within the consciousness of female existence, consciousness of female identity and independent existence, consciousness of women's individual rights, consciousness regarding opposition to patriarchal oppression and violence against women, along with consciousness of women's equal participation in politics and power structures; and within the consciousness of resistance to discrimination against women, consciousness of gender discrimination and equality, consciousness of caste and class discrimination, along with consciousness of religious and cultural discrimination, are adopted as the framework for analyzing the novel. On the basis of these diverse points of feminist trends determined in relation to the novel under discussion, through the analysis of evidence from the novel, it is concluded that consciousness of gender discrimination and equality has become vocal, as the tendency to discriminate on a gender basis, oppress, demean, and treat women as weak humans by applying various derogatory epithets simply because they are physically different is opposed in this novel. Similarly, the fact is also presented that consciousness of female existence and consciousness of opposing discrimination against women have become potent, since the convention of restricting and discriminating against women's intellect and capacity on the basis of sex in patriarchal society is also challenged, and voices are raised in favor of women's autonomy, ranging from the tendency of ensnaring women in various harmful traditions constructed by religion and culture to politics, power relations, and personal decisions. This study concludes that existentialist feminist tendencies have emerged powerfully in this novel, rewritten in alignment with the contemporary milieu using characters and events from the Mahabharata era.
british_english: In the present study, drawing on the feminist ideas put forward by the existentialist feminist Simone de Beauvoir, the feminist consciousness presented in Neelam Karki Niharika's novel Chirharan is delineated. For the feminist analysis of this novel, which presents the consciousness awakened among female and male characters against the practice of treating women as second-class citizens, consciousness of female existence and consciousness of resistance to discrimination against women are regarded as the primary bases of analysis. Within consciousness of female existence, awareness of women's identity and independent existence, awareness of women's individual rights, consciousness regarding opposition to patriarchal oppression and violence against women, alongside consciousness of women's equal participation in politics and power structures; and within consciousness of resistance to discrimination against women, consciousness of gender discrimination and equality, consciousness of caste and class discrimination, alongside consciousness of religious and cultural discrimination, are adopted as the analytical framework for the novel. On the basis of these varied points of feminist tendencies identified with respect to the novel under examination, through an analysis of textual evidence from the novel, the conclusion is reached that consciousness of gender discrimination and equality has found distinct voice, as the novel challenges the tendency to discriminate on gender grounds, oppress, belittle, and deem women inferior human beings by attaching diverse pejorative epithets simply because they are physically distinct. Furthermore, the fact is also presented that consciousness of female existence and consciousness of resistance to discrimination against women have been rendered robust, since the practice of curbing and discriminating against women's intellect and capabilities on the basis of sex in a patriarchal society is opposed, and voices are raised in support of women's freedom, extending from the entrapment of women within diverse social ills fashioned by religion and culture through to politics, power relations, and individual decision-making. This study concludes that existentialist feminist tendencies have become especially pronounced in this novel, which rewrites the characters and events of the Mahabharata era in harmony with contemporary reality.
australian_english: In this study, using the feminist ideas put forward by existentialist feminist Simone de Beauvoir as a foundation, the feminist consciousness depicted in Neelam Karki Niharika's novel Chirharan is examined. For the feminist analysis of this novel, which depicts the consciousness awakened in both female and male characters against the convention of regarding women as second-class citizens, consciousness of female existence and consciousness of opposing discrimination against women are taken as the main analytical foundations. Within consciousness of female existence, awareness of women's identity and independent existence, awareness of women's personal rights, awareness regarding resistance to patriarchal oppression and violence against women, along with awareness of women's equal participation in politics and power structures; and within consciousness of opposing discrimination against women, awareness of gender discrimination and equality, awareness of caste and class discrimination, along with awareness of religious and cultural discrimination, are taken as the framework for analysing the novel. Based on these various points of feminist tendencies set out in relation to the novel under discussion, from an analysis of textual evidence in the novel, it is concluded that awareness of gender discrimination and equality has come to the fore, since the novel challenges the practice of discriminating on gender grounds, oppressing, putting down, and treating women as weaker beings while slapping derogatory labels on them merely because of physical differences. Likewise, the study shows that consciousness of female existence and consciousness of opposing anti-women discrimination have been strengthened, given that the practice of restricting and discriminating against women's intellect and capability based on sex in a patriarchal society is challenged, and voices are raised backing women's autonomy across everything from being trapped in harmful customs manufactured by religion and culture through to politics, power dynamics, and personal choices. This study concludes that existentialist feminist tendencies have come through strongly in this novel, which reinterprets the characters and events of the Mahabharata period to match contemporary times.
informal_english: In this study, taking the feminist ideas Simone de Beauvoir put out there as a base, we're unpacking the feminist consciousness shown in Neelam Karki Niharika’s novel Chirharan. To do a proper feminist reading of this novel—which shows how both female and male characters wake up against treating women like second-class citizens—awareness of women's existence and pushing back against anti-women discrimination are taken as the main jumping-off points. Looking inside women's existence covers waking up to female identity and standing on their own two feet, backing women's individual rights, pushing back on patriarchal bashing and domestic violence, plus women getting a fair go in politics and power structures; and under opposing discrimination, waking up to gender bias and equality, caste and class bias, alongside religious and cultural discrimination, are set up as the framework to pull the novel apart. Looking at the evidence in the novel through these different feminist angles, the takeaway is that awareness of gender bias and equality really speaks up loud and clear, calling out the habit of discriminating against women, keeping them down, bagging them, and treating them like the weaker sex with all kinds of nasty labels just because their bodies are different. On top of that, the study points out that awareness of women's standing and calling out discrimination against women come through heaps stronger, since the book pushes back against boxing in and discounting women's brains and talent based on sex in a patriarchal setup, while sticking up for women calling the shots across everything from getting tangled in rotten cultural and religious habits right through to politics, power dynamics, and making up their own minds. All up, this study reckons existentialist feminist vibes come through bloody strong in this novel, which takes characters and yarns from the Mahabharata days and rewrites them to fit right into the modern world.
translator_notes: Simone de Beauvoir transliterated from Nepali 'सिमोन द बुभो'; Neelam Karki Niharika transliterated from 'नीलम कार्की निहारिका'. Strict 6-sentence order maintained across all versions. Informal flavour: New Zealand casual.
